video_title: Pablo Torre EXPOSES Kushner Lakers Purchase Story

quotes.speaker: Pablo Torre
quotes.summary_phrase: Mark Walter selling the Lakers nine months after purchase is inexplicable
quotes.excerpt: the guy who bought the team, the Lakers, the most iconic franchise maybe in the NBA, sells it
quotes.quote: I have never seen a story like this where the guy who bought the team, the Lakers, the most iconic franchise maybe in the NBA, sells it after nine months. That alone, the timeline is frankly inexplicable absent other fascinating reasons. At the same time, keep in mind that Mark Walter, who has one of my favorite superlatives, he is famously private. He was not a guy that people understood to have enough money to evaluate and purchase the Lakers at $10 billion when he bought them in the first place.

quotes.speaker: Pablo Torre
quotes.summary_phrase: Alleged undisclosed related party transaction in Mark Walter's Lakers purchase
quotes.excerpt: there was an undisclosed related party relationship and Mark Walter had said it was about $2 billion
quotes.quote: There is a thing in securities law called related party transactions where if you have a material relationship, a substantial relationship with another company, like say you also own that, you got to disclose it. And apparently, according to this whistleblower, there was an undisclosed related party relationship and Mark Walter had said it was about $2 billion in revenue. Allegedly, we are looking at 16 to 17 billion dollars.

quotes.speaker: Pablo Torre
quotes.summary_phrase: Mark Walter gave Donald Trump a World Series ring during White House visit
quotes.excerpt: he gave Donald Trump not just a jersey with his name on it, he gives him a ring
quotes.quote: He gave Donald Trump not just a jersey with his name on it, which is standard practice, he gives him a World Series ring. He put a ring on it. I asked around, I asked other owners of sports teams, have you guys ever seen the president getting a ring, a championship ring at the White House visit, and no one can recall this happening.

quotes.speaker: Pablo Torre
quotes.summary_phrase: NFL franchise valuations are skyrocketing due to big tech investment
quotes.excerpt: looks like big tech, Vinod Khosla was one of the major funders behind that one
quotes.quote: It looks like big tech, Vinod Khosla was one of the major funders behind that one. So, what do you think that means for the future of the franchises and potentially the sports themselves? Are we just going to see more of this big money coming in with the valuation than milking the fan for everything that they're worth, turning it into an ultra-luxury experience for fans?

quotes.speaker: Pablo Torre
quotes.summary_phrase: Sports revenue is primarily driven by media rights deals
quotes.excerpt: the actual bulk of revenue, of profit that teams make is on their media rights deals
quotes.quote: I think it's really important to point out that sports is not a super complicated business in the end. The actual bulk of revenue, of profit that teams make is on their media rights deals. There are lots of other ways, lots of other products and they would love to sell you jerseys and they'd love to sell you trading cards, they'd love for you to gamble and that will accrue to the bottom line, but really this is a story of an economy bolstered by media rights.

quotes.speaker: Pablo Torre
quotes.summary_phrase: The era of family-owned sports teams is ending
quotes.excerpt: we are watching the death of the family business owning these teams in real time
quotes.quote: We are watching the death of the family business owning these teams in real time. And Jeanie Buss, who was the owner of the team, it's funny, she worked out a deal with Mark Walter in recognition of that concern in which she would be still heavily involved in basketball operations. So as if the fans could trust the money guy is going to be different, but the way the team operates is going to be the same.
